name: Owen Green
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember rewriting a speech six minutes before the meal.” People around Tideline Market know Owen by a small Thursday habit. Owen picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I am their oldest friend. My speech is mostly about the groom's ex and I'm rewriting every line.
appearance: Owen is easy to recognize by a loose dark braid and fine brows over wide-set eyes. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric, Owen squares up pieces of paper while thinking when listening.
personality: Owen has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To write a speech that belongs to this couple.
family: Teri Okafor is Owen’s cousin. Owen chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Teri brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The thirteenth doughnut*, Teri says, “The thirteenth slot was a cutting mistake I was ashamed of.”
connections: Jade Cole. The old friend's speech will sound quite different if the reluctant parent comes down to listen.
